evidence_summary: 23.5% of all views carry no annotation at all: every GT 2D joint is exactly (0,0) while confidence is reported as 1.0, which is an undetected-hand sentinel rather than a measurement. Among the remaining bad views 84% fail as a whole view (>90% of joints over 50 px), and 519 frames have exactly one hand sentinel while the other is annotated, so the failure follows the hand/view rather than the camera geometry.

hypothesis: H7 hand identity swap in the 2D annotation
support_level: supported for a substantial share of non-sentinel bad views
evidence_summary: For 81% of bad views the annotation centroid is closer to the OTHER hand's projection than to its own, and in 78% it falls within one hand-width of the other hand, i.e. the annotation is sitting on the hand we did not project. Median centroid distance is 192 px to its own hand versus 16 px to the other. Residual per-joint error stays non-zero even in these cases because left and right skeletons use mirrored joint ordering, so this is a labelling problem in keypoints_2d rather than a geometry problem.

Failure is unevenly distributed across sequences (bad rate 0.05-0.27, sentinel rate 0.14-0.31), so scene content and occlusion matter. Between hands the difference is comparatively small (bad rate {'left': 0.141, 'right': 0.1596}, sentinel rate {'left': 0.2375, 'right': 0.2323}), so this is not a systematic left/right handedness bug.

hypothesis: H3 camera mapping / camera parameter mis-assignment
support_level: close to rejected as a calibration fault; camera-dependent visibility is real
evidence_summary: Per-camera bad rates span 0.00-0.98, so failure really is camera-dependent, and brics-odroid-027_cam1 is bad in 98% of its non-sentinel views. That is not evidence of a wrong camera-to-parameter mapping, because the same camera also fails to detect the hand at all in 68% of its views, and across the rig the bad rate and the sentinel rate correlate at r=0.69. A mis-assigned camera would still yield normal 2D detections and would fail on every frame; instead the cameras that project badly are those that rarely see the hand, and 24 cameras behave inconsistently from frame to frame.

hypothesis: H5 coordinate system / axis / flip misinterpretation
support_level: close to rejected (as a camera-convention fault)
evidence_summary: No mirror, axis swap or sign flip repairs the bad views (0.0% fixed). However 38.0% of bad views become consistent under a similarity transform while only 4.0% are explained by pure translation, so the annotated skeleton keeps the right shape but is placed at the wrong position and scale. In 0.8152 of bad views the other hand's 3D explains the annotation better than the nominal one. That points to the annotation naming the wrong hand or the wrong instance, not to the camera model being misread.

Sweeping the 3D frame index over t-5..t+5 for 200 bad views fixes 0.0% of them (best error still under 20 px) and only 2.0% even halve their error at a non-zero lag. A genuine constant desynchronisation would show a consistent non-zero best lag shared across views, which is not observed.

Disabling distortion changes bad views from 199.4 to 212.4 px median and repairs 0 of 200, while on good views distortion clearly helps (6.07 px on vs 11.45 px off). The distortion model is therefore being applied correctly and is not what separates good from bad views.
